chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said:
I heard Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام saying: One who has performed tayammum does not lead in prayer a people who have performed wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الْمُتَيَمِّمُ: a person who has performed tayammum, dry ablution in place of wudu
key_terms.بِقَوْمٍ: a group of people, here meaning the congregation
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: to perform prayer; here, to lead the prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a person who performed tayammum lead in prayer people who have wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling about congregational salat (prayer): a person who has performed tayammum should not lead those who are in a state of wudu (ablution). It concerns ritual purity and the qualifications for leading prayer in worship.
